# KMS Release Notes Generator

Aggregate all branch changelog files in `CHANGELOG/` into a single, compact,
human-readable release note for a given version.

**Usage**: `/kms-release-notes <version>` — e.g. `/kms-release-notes 5.3.0`

## Step 1 — Collect all branch changelogs

```bash
ls CHANGELOG/*.md
```

Read every `.md` file in `CHANGELOG/`. Ignore `CHANGELOG.md` at the repo root
(auto-generated by git-cliff — do not touch it).

## Step 2 — Parse and deduplicate entries

For each file, extract all bullet points grouped under their section headers
(`## Features`, `## Bug Fixes`, `## Security`, `## Refactor`, `## Build`,
`## CI`, `## Documentation`, `## Testing`).

**Deduplication rules:**

- If two bullets describe the same logical change (even in different wording),
  keep the more complete one and discard the other.
- If a bug fix and a feature entry describe the same item, keep under Features.
- Merge sub-sections that reference the same component (e.g. multiple `### CLI`
  blocks → one `### CLI` block).

## Step 3 — Regroup by section and component

Produce a unified structure:

```text
## Breaking Changes          ← only if any exist
## Security                  ← security fixes always first
## Features
  ### <Component>            ← group by component when ≥2 entries exist
## Bug Fixes
  ### <Component>
## Refactor                  ← summarize, not full list (see §4)
## Build
## CI
## Documentation
## Testing                   ← summarize, not full list (see §4)
```

**Component labels** (use these consistently):
`KMIP`, `API`, `CLI`, `UI`, `Crypto / FIPS`, `Database`, `HSM`, `Config`,
`WASM`, `PKCS#11`, `Nix / Packaging`, `Docs`, `CI`

**Section ordering**: Breaking Changes → Security → Features → Bug Fixes →
Refactor → Build → CI → Documentation → Testing.

## Step 4 — Compress Refactor and Testing sections

Refactor and Testing entries are internal-facing. Compress them:

- **Refactor**: replace individual bullets with one summary sentence per crate
  or area. Example: "Eliminated ~6,300 LOC of duplicate test code from
  `cosmian_kms_cli_actions`; extracted shared helpers across 8 subcommand
  modules."
- **Testing**: list only new test categories or coverage areas, not individual
  test function names.

Full detail is available per-branch in `CHANGELOG/` for contributors who need it.

## Step 5 — Cross-check SECURITY.md

If the release notes contain a `## Security` section:

1. Read `SECURITY.md`.
2. For each security entry in the release notes, verify a corresponding `COSMIAN-YYYY-NNN`
   entry exists in `SECURITY.md` with matching title and `Fixed in` version.
3. If any security entry is missing from `SECURITY.md`, **block and report**:
   > "⚠️ Security entry missing from SECURITY.md: `<title>`. Run `/security-review` to
   > generate the `COSMIAN-YYYY-NNN` entry before publishing the release notes."
4. Do **not** create `SECURITY.md` entries yourself — that is the responsibility of
   `/security-review` (Step 9). Only verify they exist.

## Step 6 — Collect PR and issue links

Scan all files for `([#N](https://github.com/Cosmian/kms/...))` patterns.
Append a deduplicated list of all referenced PR/issue numbers at the bottom under
`## References`.

Collect all `Closes #N` lines and deduplicate them.

## Step 6 — Output format

Produce the complete release note in this exact format:

```markdown
# Cosmian KMS v<VERSION> — Release Notes

> Released: <YYYY-MM-DD>

## Breaking Changes

- <migration note if any>

## Security

- <entry> ([#N](...))

## Features

### KMIP
- <entry>

### CLI
- <entry>

### API
- <entry>

## Bug Fixes

### <Component>
- <entry> ([#N](...))

## Refactor

- <one-line summary per area>

## Build

- <entry>

## References

- [#N](https://github.com/Cosmian/kms/pull/N) — <one-line description>

---
Closes #N
Closes #M
```

**Tone rules:**

- Start each bullet with a verb in imperative form: "Add", "Fix", "Remove",
  "Upgrade", "Support", "Allow", etc.
- Be specific: include type names, flag names, algorithm names, crate names
  where they help operators understand impact.
- Omit internal implementation details (macro names, LOC counts, test function
  names) unless they affect observable behavior.
- Keep the full release note under 150 lines. If it would exceed that, compress
  the Refactor and Testing sections further.

## Step 7 — Write the output

Write the release note to `CHANGELOG/RELEASE_<version>.md`.

Do **not** modify any existing `CHANGELOG/*.md` file.
Do **not** edit the root `CHANGELOG.md` (auto-generated by git-cliff).
